text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- An ASEAN conference opened in Hanoi on Tuesday to review one year's implementation of a joint action programme on the control of drug abuse through ongoing projects. It is the 19th meeting of Asian Senior Officials on Drug Matters (ASOD), but the first to be held in Vietnam.
-- Canada will provide up to $3 million to train Vietnamese decision makers in Canada.
-- At least 27 people were killed, three were injured and tens of thousands were left homeless last week when a low tropical atmospheric depression hit Vietnam's central coast.

-- Hanoi authorities moved firmly on Monday to improve safety in rail transport by ordering the removal of all obstacles along the tracks. Many houses built too close to the line that runs through the city are condemned to complete or partial destruction.

-- In a letter sent to the ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Organisation's (AIPO) 17th meeting in Thailand, Vietnamese President Le Duc Anh said Vietnam supported the expansion of ASEAN and AIPO to include Laos, Cambodia and Burma in the near future.
-- Vietnam exported 13,499 tonnes of rubber worth $19.5 million in the first eight months of 1996. For the first time 1,200 tonnes of rubber was legally exported to China.
-- City of Exchange Company of Switzerland and Vietnam's VTC Building Company are planning to build a $600 million "mini-city" on the outskirts of Hanoi.
-- Cat Bi airport in Haiphong reopened last week after a one-year shutdown for renovation.
-- A tropical depression is moving toward Vietnam's central coastal provinces of Thanh Hoa, Nghe An and Ha Tinh at a low speed and wind velocity of up to seven on the Beaufort scale.

-- The Agriculture and Rural Development Ministry said that in the first eight months of this year, the output of the farm and forestry processing industries increased by 25 percent compared with the same period of last year. Sugar production increased by 152 percent, coffee by 41.1 percent, tea by 3.0 percent and rubber by 22 percent.
-- Hanoi launched a campaign to implement the government's decision on rail and water transport safety.
-- Vietnam Airlines carried 700,000 passengers on 16,115 domestic flights in the first eight months of this year.
